consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, I'm so worried about his eyesight. He sits way too close to the TV when watching cartoons and also when reading books. I've tried to get him to move back a bit, but he says he can't see as well then.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes I call his name and he doesn't respond right away. It's like he's not hearing me or maybe just ignoring me? But if I go over to him and say it again، he'll usually answer. I don't know if it's his hearing or just him being a bit distracted.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth are a worry for me because the dentist said the enamel is weak. We have to be super careful with sugary foods and make sure he brushes them really well to prevent cavities.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: When he plays outside with friends， his breathing gets much faster than the other kids. Even when they're all running around together， my son seems to be panting more. I've mentioned it to his dad， but we haven't done anything about it yet.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Poor baby... he has low muscle tone. The physiotherapist is working with him to improve it. You can see it when he walks or tries to hold things; it's just a bit more effortful for him than for other kids his age.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Eating can be tricky sometimes. He's super fussy about food textures and won't eat certain things because of how they feel in his mouth. Like， mashed potatoes are okay but not if they're lumpy at all.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... his fingers are shorter than usual. We were told it's just something he was born with and doesn't affect anything else.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing and panting, especially when playing outside with friends.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets much faster than his peers when engaging in physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is fussy about food textures and has difficulty eating certain foods due to their texture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has low muscle tone, which affects his gait and ability to hold things.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 20-40% of individuals with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain, weakness, and urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient may have hearing difficulties, as evidenced by his delayed response to being called.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits too close to the TV and has difficulty reading books unless he is close to them, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on his teeth, requiring careful brushing and monitoring to prevent cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school and may need to attend special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than usual, which was noted at birth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth enamel and prevent cavities
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess for heart conditions
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and behavioral differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for skeletal anomalies

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue in her heart, which is being monitored through regular check-ups with a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty swallowing certain textures and often gags on her food, making feeding a challenge since birth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced developmental delay as a baby, being slower to sit, stand, and walk compared to other kids, and has been diagnosed with a neurological condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient likes the TV volume really loud, suggesting possible hearing sensitivity, and has been diagnosed with conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board in class, even when sitting up front, and often squints and rubs her eyes during lessons.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity, especially with cold foods, and has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing problems may affect her learning, and she may require extra support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced developmental delay as a baby and may have ongoing developmental challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a bit of a curve in her back, which the orthopedic doctor is monitoring, and has short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor the patient's heart condition
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for spinal and skeletal abnormalities
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's developmental and behavioural challenges
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular monitoring of the patient's curve in her back and short fingers to prevent further complications

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition that requires regular monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion, making mealtime challenging and affecting her ability to eat a balanced diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, taking longer to master simple tasks like tying shoes or riding a bike, and sometimes trips over her own feet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has selective hearing, where she picks up on certain sounds but completely misses others, even when they're loud.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, which is bothering her lately.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, making her more prone to cavities, and her parents are keeping a close eye on her dental health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development has been slow, and her parents are concerned about the potential impact on her education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues and slow speech development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with shorter fingers than typical.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's weak enamel and prevent cavities.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's selective hearing and prevent conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to address the patient's blurry vision.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address the patient's coordination issues and slow speech development.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fatigue easily during physical activities and has difficulty keeping up with peers, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slower weight gain compared to peers, despite a good appetite, and experiences feeding difficulties with harder foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences brief episodes of staring off into space and unresponsiveness, suggesting potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV very high and may have difficulty hearing, especially in noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board at school, especially when the teacher writes in small letters or from a distance, and squints or leans forward to get a better look.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty chewing harder foods and often avoids them or asks for them to be cut into smaller pieces.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was diagnosed with hip dysplasia, requiring monitoring and physiotherapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health and address any concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect any potential hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate heart health.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess bone health and development.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address any concerns.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences irregular bowel movements, and managing her diet helps alleviate some discomfort but it remains an ongoing concern.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in babies with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding, and a very small number needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires easily during physical tasks, even simple exercises leave her drained, and she has noticeable speech delay and struggles to articulate her thoughts clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have developmental delay, with the degree ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is overwhelmed by loud noises and gets frustrated easily in crowded or noisy areas.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism and needs glasses to see clearly, with challenges in finding the right prescription.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint, with treatment including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth require more maintenance than average, with frequent dental visits necessary to prevent cavities and ensure her teeth remain healthy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech delay and difficulties articulating her thoughts clearly impact her daily interactions and academic performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school, but some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to prevent cavities and ensure healthy teeth
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support the patient's development and daily functioning.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve abnormality in his heart that requires regular monitoring by a cardiologist to prevent major issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had poor feeding in infancy, which made it challenging for him to eat properly and gain weight at a normal rate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems less coordinated when moving compared to his peers, taking longer to master simple tasks like tying shoelaces or riding a bike.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV very high to hear it properly, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia (far-sightedness), which affects his daily life, especially in school where he struggles to see the board clearly, and he uses glasses to correct this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring caution with food and avoiding hard items to prevent further damage.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's hypermetropia and potential hearing difficulties may impact his educational experience, particularly in settings where visual and auditory cues are crucial.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) in secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced delayed fontanelle closure and takes longer to reach milestones than expected, requiring patience and tailored support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe, with most children having some degree of developmental delay and behavioural differences.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), and an increased risk of scoliosis.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent enamel damage.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct and manage vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental delays and coordination issues.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often turning the TV volume up too high, and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, with eyes that seem to get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has frequent dental problems, including cavities and toothaches, requiring regular dentist visits.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns

Parent: Chewing has become a challenge for him lately. Harder foods like apples or meat are difficult for him to manage. We've had to adjust his diet somewhat to softer foods to make mealtime less stressful.

Parent: Physical activity... he just can't seem to keep up with the other kids. Even simple games like tag or running around leave him winded and tired quickly. It worries me that there might be an underlying issue we need to address.

Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: The tethered cord issue is something we're closely monitoring. The specialists have assured us they're on top of it, but it's still a concern for us as parents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Parent: Well... aside from what we've discussed, his movements are slightly different from his peers. And he was diagnosed with scoliosis. These are things we're working through with his therapists and doctors to ensure he gets the right support and care.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty keeping up with physical activities and gets winded easily, suggesting potential underlying cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, with mealtime often being a struggle, and experiences days where eating is hard or he's not interested in food.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a lack of interest in feeding being a significant and long-lasting issue for some.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue that is being closely monitored by specialists, and also experiences difficulties with movements that are slightly different from his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, and some may have neurological differences or developmental delays.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing certain sounds and often asks for the TV volume to be turned up, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, squints, or rubs his eyes frequently, indicating potential eyesight issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods like apples or meat, and has to adjust his diet to softer foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's movements are slightly different from his peers, and he was diagnosed with scoliosis, indicating potential developmental differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delays, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with some requiring medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis and experiences difficulties with movements.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, with some experiencing hip dysplasia or delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems and provide appropriate treatment
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to investigate potential heart conditions
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor bone health and development
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental needs
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular check-ups with specialists to monitor and manage tethered cord issue and scoliosis

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily when playing with friends or running around, can't seem to keep up like others her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky about food and will only eat certain things, which can make mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Coordination seems a bit off sometimes; she trips over her own feet or drops things more often than her siblings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media, so the family has had to deal with ear infections from time to time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board in class, which makes learning a bit harder for her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Cold foods make her teeth hurt, so she avoids them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision problems make learning a bit harder for her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider a palate review to monitor for subtle anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and coordination
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

Parent: Well, we've noticed he seems to hear some sounds but not others clearly. For instance, if we're watching TV together, he'll respond to loud noises but sometimes doesn't react to softer voices or certain tones. It's like he's picking and choosing what he wants to listen to, but I'm not sure if that's normal or not.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: He's been complaining about tooth sensitivity lately, especially when he eats cold food like ice cream or cold drinks. He says it hurts and makes him jump. We've tried using special toothpaste, but it doesn't seem to make much difference.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes... the doctors found a septal defect. They said it's a hole in the heart that didn't close properly after birth. We go for regular check-ups to monitor it and make sure it doesn't cause more serious problems. It's been a worry for us since the diagnosis.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He has these episodes where he just stares off into space. It's like he's in a trance or something. We call them his 'blank spells'. They can happen anytime - during play, while eating... it's really frightening because we never know when they'll happen. And sometimes he gets rigid and unresponsive for a few seconds before snapping back to reality.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Constipation has been an issue for him. He struggles to go to the bathroom regularly and when he does, it's often very painful for him. We've tried changing his diet and encouraging more fluid intake but nothing seems to work consistently.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: There are two main things. Firstly, the delayed fontanelle closure has been a concern since birth. The doctors have been monitoring it closely to ensure it doesn't lead to further complications. Secondly, he struggles with clarity when trying to talk. His words aren't always clear, and he gets frustrated when we can't understand him. It's heartbreaking to see him try so hard to communicate but not being able to express himself properly.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect, a hole in the heart that didn't close properly after birth, which requires regular monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation and struggles to go to the bathroom regularly, with painful bowel movements.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has episodes of staring off into space, described as 'blank spells', which can happen anytime, and sometimes becomes rigid and unresponsive for a few seconds before snapping back to reality.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty hearing some sounds but not others clearly, and seems to pick and choose what he wants to listen to.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board at school, often squints, and rubs his eyes, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, especially when eating cold food or drinks, and has been complaining about it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing difficulties may affect his learning, as he struggles to see the board and hear the teacher clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and the extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed fontanelle closure and struggles with clarity when trying to talk, which can be frustrating for him.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, and the degree of delay ranges from mild to severe.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed fontanelle closure, which has been a concern since birth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing difficulties
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess any skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and daily life
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular monitoring of the patient's neurological episodes and adjustment of treatment as necessary

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that is managed with regular check-ups and medication, allowing him to be active without significant restrictions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, some of which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems from time to time, which are noticeable and uncomfortable for him.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and bowel issues can be common, with some children requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding and others having long-lasting lack of interest in feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets exhausted quicker than his peers during playtime or when running around, and there are concerns about delayed fontanelle closure.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and there can be varying degrees of developmental delay and intellectual disability.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond right away when called, suggesting possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, corrected with glasses, which helps him see distant objects more clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than usual, which could lead to orthodontic issues later on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended, especially for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally behind his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but possibly requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans for secondary education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally delayed and seems to tire easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: There are concerns about delayed fontanelle closure.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and enamel health.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in the first few years, to address any conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to correct any vision problems such as myopia or astigmatism.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to assess heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to evaluate bone age and detect any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental delays and behavioural differences.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition that requires regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is slower to gain weight compared to his friends, and his parents monitor his eating habits closely to ensure he's getting enough nutrients.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences moments where he stares off into space for a few seconds, which is unsettling because it looks like he's not responding to anything around him during those times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has selective hearing, where he picks up on some noises just fine but struggles with softer sounds.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means he has trouble seeing things that are far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are not very strong and break or chip easily, requiring careful monitoring of his diet and regular brushing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's fontanelle did not close properly, and the doctors are keeping an eye on it to see how it develops over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent further damage
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and adjust treatment as necessary
* Regular eyesight reviews to monitor the patient's vision and adjust treatment as necessary
* Regular cardiac check-ups to monitor the patient's heart condition and adjust treatment as necessary
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and behaviour
* Monitoring of the patient's growth velocity and consideration of referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular monitoring of the patient's fontanelle to ensure proper closure and development.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than other kids his age, even after a short playtime outside or a brisk walk, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Mealtimes can be challenging, with the patient being finicky about what he eats and sometimes not wanting to eat at all.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a lack of interest in feeding being significant and long-lasting in some cases.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with a potential tethered cord, which could cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat themselves because he didn't catch what they said the first time, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple aeration tube insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often complains about squinting when he looks at things, especially when reading or watching TV, and his eyes get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint, with treatment including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had some complaints about tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods like ice cream or cold drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, with careful brushing being very important and regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most going to a mainstream primary school, but some requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a noticeably different posture compared to his peers, and his testicles didn't descend properly, which is being monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, with babies sometimes experiencing a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for spinal and skeletal issues
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address any delays or difficulties.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily and is out of breath quickly, indicating possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has bowel movement concerns, including accidents and trouble with regular bowel movements.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and must take medication regularly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear recently, which affected her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things clearly, possibly due to astigmatism.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble chewing harder foods and may have weak enamel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developing slower than other kids her age, which may impact her educational needs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developing slower than other kids her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia, which requires careful management to prevent further issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of the spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and enamel health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to confirm astigmatism and provide corrective measures
* Cardiac review to assess heart condition and provide appropriate management
* Referral for a skeletal review to monitor for hip dysplasia and other skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental needs
* Regular monitoring of bowel movements and adjustment of diet or treatment as necessary
* Continued management and monitoring of epilepsy to prevent seizures and adjust medication as necessary

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve abnormality in his heart, which is being monitored regularly to ensure it does not impact his daily life or activity levels.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is managed with dietary changes and occasional medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are being managed with medication, and regular adjustments are made as needed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had a glue ear in the past, which caused temporary hearing issues, but his hearing has returned to normal after treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means he has difficulty seeing distant objects clearly, and is due for another assessment to monitor the progression.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been experiencing tooth sensitivity, especially when eating cold foods, and has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor any changes in hearing
* Regular monitoring of the patient's heart condition to ensure it does not impact daily life or activity levels
* Continued management of seizures with medication and regular adjustments as needed
* Monitoring of constipation and adjustment of dietary changes and medication as needed
* Follow-up appointments to assess any developments or necessary interventions for palatal abnormalities
* Regular monitoring of the patient's vision to assess any changes or progression of myopia

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has hypermetropia, which means she has a higher than normal curvature of her eyeball. This affects how she sees things at close range and makes reading and focusing more difficult. She often squints when looking at books or toys up close.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our child gets easily frustrated in noisy environments. It's not that she can't hear well; it's just that the loud noises overwhelm her. In quieter settings, she responds appropriately to sounds and voices.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth have weak enamel. We have to ensure she brushes them carefully and regularly visits the dentist for check-ups to prevent any further issues. The dentist has also recommended a special toothpaste to help strengthen her teeth.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Due to a pre-existing condition, our child needs regular heart check-ups with a specialist. These check-ups monitor her heart health and ensure everything remains stable. So far‚ these have been routine and haven't indicated any major concerns.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain‚ nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Developmentally‚ she has been slower to reach certain milestones‚ such as walking or sitting unassisted. While she eventually achieves these milestones‚ it takes her longer than her peers. We work closely with physical therapists to support her development.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ she experiences bowel problems. This includes constipation and occasional diarreah. Managing her diet and ensuring she stays hydrated helps alleviate these issues to some extent.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the mentioned conditions‚ our child struggles with speech clarity. She finds it hard to express herself clearly‚ which can be frustrating for her. Additionally‚ she has a delayed fontanelle closure‚ where her soft palate doesn't move properly during speech‚ affecting her pronunciation. These are areas we're working on with speech therapists.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and developmental delay is reported in almost all children with the syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets easily frustrated in noisy environments due to sensitivity to loud noises, but responds appropriately to sounds and voices in quieter settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects her close-range vision and makes reading and focusing more difficult, and she often squints when looking at books or toys up close.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome can have a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's developmental delays and speech clarity issues may impact her educational progress and require specialized support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and requires physical therapy to support her development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a delayed fontanelle closure.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's weak enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and address any concerns
* Eyesight review to monitor the patient's vision and address any concerns
* Regular heart check-ups with a specialist to monitor the patient's heart health
* Physical therapy to support the patient's developmental delays
* Speech therapy to address the patient's speech clarity issues
* Behavioral therapy to address any behavioral concerns
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and educational support to address the patient's developmental delays and educational needs.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a condition with his back when born, where the cord was stuck, and now he's slow at learning new things.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient likes TV loud, indicating possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, where he can see far away things too close.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: Cold things hurt the patient's teeth, like ice cream or cold water.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes a long time to learn things, and other kids his age do more things than him already.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient is slow at learning new things.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, and some have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Cardiac review to monitor for heart conditions

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation and bowel movement challenges, requiring careful monitoring of her diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with hypotonia, characterized by weaker muscles than typical for her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear last year, requiring treatment, and may be prone to recurrent otitis media or conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes frequently when trying to focus, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is prone to cavities and requires more frequent dental visits than average kids.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often experience dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or utilize Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often exhibit behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than usual and stands and walks with a noticeably different posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome experience skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curvature of the 5th fingers, and hip dysplasia.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect potential hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess skeletal anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address challenges
